battlecards.why_selected: Provided improved transportation and surcharge discounts without service disruption; agreed to waive late fees until June 2023 and to continue credit-card billing through 2025.
battlecards.contract_terms: Amended Transportation Services Agreement; late-fee waiver through Jun-2023; credit-card billing terms locked through 2025; dimensional factor retained at 210; no term commitment beyond existing agreement.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of moving volume to UPS GPO program, detailed shipment-level benchmarking, and demonstrated savings opportunities on ground minimums and surcharges.
supplier_strengths: Willingness to reduce ground minimums and surcharges
supplier_weaknesses: Limited flexibility on Express service discounts
battlecards.switching_costs: Medium – would require label re-routing, system changes, and customer communication if switched.
battlecards.notes: Earned and base discounts as well as surcharge caps were the primary focus areas; negotiation completed May-2022.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match FedEx’s revised ground minimums and surcharge concessions; switching costs for full conversion deemed too high for limited incremental savings.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used as competitive benchmark to pressure FedEx; leveraged Treya UPS GPO rates in analysis.
supplier_strengths: Competitive GPO pricing on select service levels
supplier_weaknesses: Lower integration with CJPP shipping systems
Would require carrier diversification across facilities
battlecards.switching_costs: High – system integration, label changes, staff retraining.
battlecards.notes: Maintained as secondary carrier for limited volume; annual spend historically <10% of parcel costs.

battlecards.why_selected: Delivered best pricing on exact-match items for Harrisburg facility and agreed to 2%30-Net60 terms improving cash flow.
battlecards.contract_terms: Memorandum of Understanding executed Apr-2022; pricing fixed for 12 months with quarterly review; 2% early-pay discount, Net60 standard.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive RFP with alternative supplier pricing and commitment to consolidate volumes at Harrisburg plant.
supplier_weaknesses: Limited design/structural services vs national converters
battlecards.switching_costs: Low-to-medium; would require re-qualification of box specs and delivery schedules.
battlecards.notes: Savings exclude additional $6.5K available through early-payment discount.

battlecards.why_selected: Maintained service continuity in Las Vegas with modest price reduction and acceptance of 1%10-Net45 terms.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU executed Mar-2022; annual price review aligned to industry indices; 1%/10 Net45 early-pay option.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat to shift volume to other regional converters and consolidated box SKUs.
supplier_strengths: Established delivery routes to Vegas DC
supplier_weaknesses: Small savings achieved due to tight West Coast capacity
battlecards.switching_costs: Medium – alternate vendors would require freight from CA or AZ increasing transit time.
battlecards.notes: Additional $3.96K savings available through early-payment discount not included in headline figure.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided best-and-final offer with 22% reduction and agreed to maintain local inventory levels for Harrisburg site.
battlecards.contract_terms: Contract executed Apr-28-2022; pricing locked for 12 months; inventory review every 90 days.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of awarding volume to Sigma Supply plus consolidation of SKUs.
supplier_weaknesses: Historically higher pricing prior to negotiation
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – same product specs across vendors, but change would disrupt just-in-time delivery schedules.
battlecards.notes: Colony retained Harrisburg while Sigma awarded Las Vegas facility.

battlecards.why_selected: Offered 32% category savings overall and provided 3PL warehouse in Hershey, PA with no financial penalties for >120-day inventory.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU fully executed Mar-2022; pricing fixed for first 12 months; stocking program with 120-day turnover policy.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to split award between regions and threat to incumbent pricing in Las Vegas.
supplier_weaknesses: New relationship – operational performance yet to be proven
battlecards.switching_costs: Low initially, but increases with inventory commitments held at Sigma facilities.
battlecards.notes: Savings dollars derived as residual category savings after Colony award; exact baseline spend by site not provided.

battlecards.why_selected: Access to OMNIA GPO rates delivering 13% savings and standardized markup structure; ability to serve both PA and NV warehouses.
battlecards.contract_terms: Participation Agreement executed Aug-2022; markups fixed for 24 months with market wage reviews; no minimum hours commitment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Volume leverage aggregated through OMNIA; benchmarking of historical markups against GPO ceiling rates.
supplier_weaknesses: Initial misalignment on PA wage rates caused communication issues
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – would require onboarding new agency staff and retraining supervisors.
battlecards.notes: CJPP net savings after Treya distribution estimated at 8%.
